item.title: Vinoo Mankad trophy: Dravid slams 151 as Karnataka chase down 358; Sehwag scores 173 off 143 balls in losing cause
item.description: Anvay Dravid, younger son of former India cricketer Rahul Dravid, scored 151 off 100 balls to help Karnataka chase down Gujarat’s target of 358 with five wickets to spare in the Vinoo Mankad Trophy Elite tournament. Leading Karnataka in the tournament, the 17-year-old played a key role in the chase, combining with Dhruv Krishnan to guide his team to victory. Anvay is captaining a 16-member Karnataka squad in the tournament, which began in Visakhapatnam earlier this month. His appointment as captain comes 10 months after he made his India U19 debut against Afghanistan in Sri Lanka in November last year. Anvay had also impressed in Karnataka’s previous match against Delhi, scoring 85 off just 41 balls. He combined with Rohith Reddy, Nitish Arya and Dhruv Krishnan to help Karnataka post 418 after being asked to bat first. Gujarat, meanwhile, got off to a difficult start after being put in to bat, losing their first wicket at 19 in the seventh over. Shaurya Pancholi and Ved Patel then steadied the innings with a 66-run partnership for the second wicket. Gujarat soon slipped to 100/3, but Kush Patel and Sameer Bhandari added 40 runs for the fourth wicket. After Kush was dismissed in the 31st over, Sameer and Yash Panjwani put together a 217-run partnership for the fifth wicket to take Gujarat to 357. In reply, Rohith and Nitish added 30 runs for the opening wicket before Nitish was dismissed in the sixth over. Rohith and Krishnan then put on 33 runs for the second wicket, but Rohith departed in the 12th over. Krishnan and Anvay took charge from there, adding 204 runs for the third wicket to bring Karnataka closer to the target. Krishnan was dismissed in the 38th over, after which Anvay added 61 runs with Aniketh Reddy for the fourth wicket before losing his wicket in the 44th over. Aniketh and Tejas Reddy then completed the chase to seal Karnataka’s five-wicket win. Aaryavir Sehwag scores 173 off 143 balls Former India opener Virender Sehwag’s elder son, Aaryavir, also made headlines in the Vinoo Mankad Trophy Elite tournament, scoring 173 off 143 balls for Delhi. However, his effort was not enough to secure a win, as Chandigarh chased down the target to win by five wickets in the 42nd over. Aaryavir, 18, is captaining a 16-member Delhi squad in the tournament, which began in Visakhapatnam on October 8. His appointment as captain came shortly after he made his India U19 debut against Australia in Rajkot in September. Batting first, Delhi finished at 289/6 in 50 overs, with Aaryavir and fellow opener Arnav Bugga, who scored 47, accounting for much of the team’s runs. Chandigarh made light work of the chase, reaching the target in the 42nd over. Rupesh Yadav led the way with 167 off 125 balls, hitting five sixes and 23 boundaries to help Chandigarh register a five-wicket victory. 134998774

item.title: Oregon Basketball Recap: Seattle University
item.description: Oregon interim head coach Tony Stubblefield, center, rallies his team as the Oregon Ducks host the Seattle University Redhawks on Oct. 15, 2026, at Matthew Knight Arena in Eugene, Oregon. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Your new-look Oregon Ducks took on the Seattle University Thunderbirds on Thursday evening, in an exhibition matchup. It was the first chance to get a look at the basketball team since longtime HC Dana Altman abruptly retired on October 7th. The Ducks jumped out to an early 5-0 lead to start things off, but quickly found themselves trailing 12-5 with 13 minutes left in the half. Oregon would claw back into things to tie the game up at 19-19 with 8:24 left in the half, and it would remain a back-and-forth game until the half, where the Ducks would hold a 36-35 lead. Over the first 6 minutes of the 2nd half, the Ducks would go on a 17-5 run to take a 53-40 lead with 14:08 left in the game. But, that’s where things would begin to fall apart for Oregon. Over the next 7-ish minutes, Seattle would go on a big run of their own to take a 59-56 lead with 7 minutes remaining. They would not trail again, and would end up beating the Ducks 71-65. Final at MKA. #GoDucks pic.twitter.com/uWu9eaOUkE — Oregon Men's Basketball (@OregonMBB) October 16, 2026 Well… that could’ve gone better. Obviously, it’s just a pre-season/exhibition game, but I was still a little disappointed in the result. I will give interim head coach Tony Stubblefield the benefit of the doubt, considering the circumstances, but I think this game was a perfect opportunity to instill a bit of confidence into the fan base, and unfortunately the team fell short. Largely, the offense looked… fine. I liked a lot of the motion in the half-court, when they were able to actually run their sets. Seattle just played fast and sped the game up, making it hard to get into the offense. One big thing they need to work on is free-throw shooting. The team got to the line a good amount of times, but went just 18-27. That’s 9 points left on the table, in a game where they lost by 6. Hopefully in the next showing against the Utah Utes (on Wednesday the 21st) we’ll be able to see some real improvement. As always, ‘Sco Ducks.

item.title: The Washington Nationals Were Dangerous On The Base Paths In 2026
item.description: CLEVELAND, OH - MAY 27: Travis Bazzana (37) of the Cleveland Guardians tries to hold onto the ball as James Wood (29) of the Washington Nationals steals second base during an MLB game on May 27, 2026 at Progressive Field in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Joe Robbins/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images For Nationals fans accustomed to watching promising innings disappear on the basepaths, 2026 offered a welcome change. The Nats played aggressive baseball, but with better results. Stealing bases and taking the extra bag became meaningful strengths, giving them another way to generate offense. The improvement also deserves to be counted among the successes of manager Blake Butera’s coaching staff, particularly first-base and baserunning coach Corey Ray. The Nats finished with 178 stolen bases and 40 caught stealings, succeeding on 81.7% of their attempts. In 2025, the Nationals stole 132 bases and were caught 48 times, a 73.3% success rate. That means they added 46 steals while making eight fewer outs trying to steal. More attempts produced substantially better efficiency. The comparison with 2024 is revealing, too. That team piled up 223 steals but was caught 73 times, converting 75.3% of its attempts. The Nats 2026 club finished with fewer steals, but its success rate was more than six percentage points higher. There is value in putting pressure on the defense. There is also value in keeping a runner available for the next hitter. Nasim Nunez just broke the Nationals' record for stolen bases in a season with his 48th. He swiped third moments later for his 49th bag of the year. Nunez leads the major leagues. pic.twitter.com/Gtr4PwwYLo — Grant Paulsen (@GrantPaulsen) September 23, 2026 The progress extended beyond stealing. Baseball-Reference’s extra-base-taken percentage measures how frequently runners advance more than one base on a single or more than two on a double when opportunities arise. The Nats rate climbed from 40% in 2025 to 47% in 2026, exceeding its 45% mark from 2024 as well. Those advances can turn an ordinary single into a first-and-third situation or bring a runner home without requiring another hit. Advanced metrics reinforce the picture. Baseball-Reference credited the Nationals with nine baserunning runs above average in 2026, with another six runs credited separately for avoiding double plays. These measures put a run value on contributions that batting average and home run totals miss. The Nats were creating advantages between contact and the next plate appearance. FanGraphs’ BsR, which expresses baserunning value in runs above average, also shows how widely those contributions were distributed. item.title: Bears vs. Falcons Injury Report: Caleb Williams is Questionable
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears stands on the sideline during the national anthem prior to the game against the Minnesota Vikings at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears and the Atlanta Falcons have released their game-day injury reports, and there’s good news for both starting quarterbacks. Chicago’s Caleb Williams (hamstring) logged a third straight full practice, while Atlanta’s Michael Penix Jr. also practiced fully all week after leaving his last game with a rib injury. item.title: Dodgers facing tricky question over Shohei Ohtani's future as a two-way player
item.description: Dodgers facing tricky question over Shohei Ohtani's future as a two-way player originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The 2026 season has come to an end for the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS, as they were swept by the Milwaukee Brewers in four games. Plenty of things went wrong in this series, but one of the biggest storylines was the struggles of two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani . But since he wasn't pitching due to injury, Ohtani stuck as a DH-only. Now, heading into the offseason, ESPN's Alden Gonzalez pointed out the big question the Dodgers will have with Ohtani. Unfortunately, they must try to figure out whether he can truly be a two-way player going forward, as his injury this year was a huge loss. Dodgers have tricky Shohei Ohtani question to answer "The big question will be whether Ohtani will continue to pitch," Gonzalez writes. "Assuming he does, what exactly will that look like in his age-32 season, coming off a year in which pain in his left knee and right bicep kept him away from the rotation after early July?" Ohtani was an elite pitcher in the first half of the 2026 MLB season. But after an injury sidelined him in July, his attempt to return to the mound didn't go well, and he was forced to focus fully on being a hitter for Los Angeles. Now, as Gonzalez highlighted, the Dodgers have a question of whether or not Ohtani can keep pitching. It's hard to imagine Ohtani giving up on pitching, so the next question is how the Dodgers will actually utilize Ohtani as a pitcher. MORE : How Mets could have advantage over Dodgers in free-agent pursuit of Tarik Skubal Is Ohtani going to remain a full-time starter, getting in as much work as possible as he did in the first half of 2026? Or will the Dodgers limit his workload by either using him as an opener or maybe even as a reliever? After Ohtani's third season with the team on a 10-year deal, these aren't the type of questions the Dodgers hoped they would be forced to answer. Ohtani is a great hitter, but his best value comes as a two-way player, which might be difficult to accomplish after an injury-riddled second half of 2026, and he will be 32 years old in 2027. This is a very interesting question for the Dodgers, and one that fans should be paying close attention to this offseason and leading up to the regular season. It's probably too soon for Ohtani to totally give up on pitching, but it's, unfortunately, becoming a real question he and the Dodgers will have to answer at the end of every regular season going forward. item.title: Real Madrid demand Javier Tebas resignation after Nazi propaganda comparison
item.description: Real Madrid have called for LaLiga president Javier Tebas to immediately resign after he accused the club of employing techniques used by Nazi propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels . Real and Tebas have clashed on a number of occasions this season , with the league chief’s remarks in an X post on Friday appearing to be the final straw for the club. “The repeated conduct of Javier Tebas shows a lack of neutrality, respect and impartiality incompatible with his institutional responsibilities,” a club statement read. “Real Madrid CF considers it absolutely intolerable and extraordinarily serious that someone who occupies two positions of utmost responsibility in Spanish football should resort to a comparison with the propaganda methods of the Nazi regime to discredit our club, its management and its television. “His constant attacks on Real Madrid and those who demand transparency and regeneration constitute, in the opinion of our club, a real scourge for Spanish football.” Real called for his immediate resignation from his LaLiga position, and from his vice-presidency of the Spanish football federation (RFEF). The club said it was “especially concerning” that Tebas referenced the Negreira case in the X post. Real have handed a dossier to Uefa about the case, which centres on payments from Barcelona to Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira, the former vice-president of the Spanish Football Federation’s technical committee of referees (CTA). Barcelona say the payments were for scouting and technical reports provided by Negreira on officials, but it has been alleged previously that the money was being used to bribe referees. Real Madrid president Florentino Perez has been outspoken about the Negreira case (Getty) Real said: “It is particularly significant that Javier Tebas….dedicates his efforts to discrediting Real Madrid instead of promoting, from his institutional responsibilities, the clarification of these very serious facts and the necessary regeneration of Spanish football.” Tebas’ post accused journalists of acting as the “official mouthpiece” for the club to air grievances and added: “Real Madrid’s management directs an orchestra of mouthpieces and Real Madrid TV leads the singing. “Their score is always the same: select the plays that suit them, repeat the grievance, feed the suspicion, and point fingers at the enemies. That method recalls propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels: systematic repetition, construction of an enemy, and subordination of facts to the narrative.” He added: “The comparison is with those propaganda techniques, not with an ideology or, of course, with the Madridista fanbase.” Real, however, responded: “The clarification that he is not referring to Nazi ideology does not mitigate the deeply offensive, morally repugnant, and institutionally unworthy nature of his statements.” PA

item.title: Kevin Willard Passing On Recruiting High School Players: Is It The Right Move?
item.description: It is a new era of college basketball with the transfer portal and NIL becoming king. This means coaches have to think differently as well, especially with the NCAA bringing in the new fifth-year rule. Villanova’s Kevin Willard has done this and that includes passing on recruiting high school players this year in hopes of bringing back his players eligible for a fifth year. “We’re not recruiting a high school kid this year… just because of the fifth-year rule,” Willard said at Big East Media Day. “We have six guys that can come back for a fifth year. So, I’d much rather have one of my players come back, than bring in a high school kid.” The new age-based model gives athletes five years of eligibility to play in five years. This window begins when the athlete begins college or during the academic year after they turn 19 years old. “I think moving forward, this kind of reminds me of what happened with COVID,” Willard said. “A lot of high school kids, a lot of high school players, got penalized, and it wasn’t their fault. So I think after a year or two, this system will flush out and I think coaches will go back to recruiting high school players.” It was a busy offseason for Willard and the Wildcats. After losing the entire roster minus Tyler Perkins and Matt Hodge, Willard was tasked with retooling in hopes of competing in the Big East. Safe to say he did that in the transfer portal along with bringing in Adam Oumiddich from the high school ranks. When looking at the roster, led by Luigi Suigo and Kwame Evans Jr. in the frontcourt, it is clear that Villanova is set to compete this year. Willard made it clear that this is not a longterm plan but with the way this team is built, it makes more sense to focus on the portal and re-recruiting his own players rather than hitting high schools. Unfortunately, this is the bed that the NCAA made — not Willard and Villanova. It is important for the Wildcats to get back to winning and after year one, Willard as the team going in the right direction.

item.title: Red Sox could match rare feat with three Gold Glove winners
item.description: Three Red Sox position players were named Gold Glove award finalists Wednesday. Right fielder Wilyer Abreu and center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela were both chosen as nominees after winning the award last year. In addition, Caleb Durbin was a first-time nominee at third base. The Sox had three finalists last year, too, with catcher Carlos Narváez joining Abreu and Rafaela as nominees. Abreu has won the award two years running and could become a three-time honoree when the winners are revealed next month. He led all major league right fielders with 13 assists while being credited with 28 defensive runs saved. Toronto’s Nathan Lukes and Houston’s Cam Smith are the two other finalists in right field. Should Abreu win again, only five players in franchise history will have won more Gold Gloves: Dwight Evans (eight), Carl Yastrzemski (seven), Dustin Pedroia (four), Mookie Betts (four) and Fred Lynn (four). Rafaela, a first-time winner a year ago, led all American League center fielders with eight assists while recording 21 defensive runs saved. He also led all American League outfielders with 17 outs above average, second in the game only to the Chicago Cubs’ Pete Crow-Armstrong (26). He’ll be contending for the honor with Steven Kwan of the Cleveland Guardians and Evan Carter of the Texas Rangers in center. In his first season with the Red Sox, Durbin struggled mightily at the plate for the first half of the season, but his play in the field never faltered in the infield. He was credited with six outs above average at third base. The other AL finalists at third base are Minnesota’s Brooks Lee and Kansas City’s Nick Loftin. The only other third baseman in team history to win a Gold Glove is Frank Malzone, who won three straight from 1957-1959. Should all three Red Sox finalists win the award, it will mark the first time since 2018 that three players on the Boston roster have been honored. That year, outfielders Jackie Bradley Jr. and Mookie Betts along with second baseman Ian Kinsler were winners. The Sox also had three winners in 2011: First baseman Adrian Gonzalez, second baseman Dustin Pedroia and outfielder Jacoby Ellsbury. item.title: Shohei Ohtani Leaves Door Open to Offseason Surgery After Dodgers Injury Battles
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers designated hitter Shohei Ohtani is unsure whether to undergo offseason surgery to address his injuries. Will Shohei Ohtani have surgery? Ohtani has battled right bicep, left knee, and neck discomfort/inflammation since the summer, playing through it all until the final game of the season. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) When asked about a procedure or work, Ohtani has always deferred that decision to the offseason. Now that the Dodgers season is over after their 6-4 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers, Ohtani was asked about a potential offseason procedure to address all of his prevailing injuries. “Hard to tell at this point,” Ohtani said, via translator Will Ireton. “It’s something that’s going to be analyzed, discussed over the offseason, and see if that’s a viable thing to do.” Oct 15, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers designated hitter Shohei Ohtani (17) celebrates with teammates after hitting a three-run home run during the second inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game four of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images What Ohtani learned from these injuries Meanwhile, Ohtani is left processing how the season ended and trying to break down what led to his run of injuries and health issues. “I haven’t been able to really come to grip in terms of what I’ve learned overall this season,” he said. “It’s something that I’m going to kind of go back to the drawing board in terms of treatment, training program, and see what I can come up with for next season.” Oct 15, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers designated hitter Shohei Ohtani (17) reacts after hitting a three-run home run during the second inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game four of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images There is plenty to be proud of for Ohtani, who was on track to have the greatest season ever, finishing the season as an elite pitcher and hitter. However, his push for greatness came with consequences down the line, and he will need to manage his body if he wants to hold up now that he is entering his mid-30s. Given Ohtani’s competitive drive and work ethic, he’ll keep pushing himself to the limit, but this year reminds us what happens when he goes beyond it.

item.title: Thunder drops official statement regarding Spanish club attempting to block Aday Mara’s playing in 2026
item.description: Credit: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images Thunder drops official statement regarding Spanish club attempting to block Aday Mara’s playing in 2026 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coach Mark Daigneault ’s Oklahoma City Thunder is preparing for the season opener on October 20 at San Antonio and hoping center Aday Mara can break a run of terrible rookie injury luck . The Thunder are a popular NBA championship pick by GMs around the league and Mara’s stellar preseason play is a big reason why. Mara is expected to be in uniform for the opener, but his former Spanish club Zaragoza has threatened to block him from playing, saying he is under contract for the 2026-27 season. The club said it has not received a request for international transfer and would block one if such a move was made. The Thunder released a statement on the matter according to NBA writer Marc Stein. “Aday last played three years of NCAA college basketball and therefore, as advised by the NBA, no clearance from the Spanish team is required to play in the NBA,” a Thunder spokesperson said according to Stein. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Mara was selected with the 12th overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft after leading Michigan to the NCAA men’s basketball national championship. He averaged 12.1 points per game and shot 66.8% from the field for former Wolverines coach Dusty May’s team, becoming one of three lottery picks among his teammates including Morez Johnson Jr. of the Dallas Mavericks and Yaxel Lendeborg of the Golden State Warriors. The Thunder lost rookie guard Otega Oweh to a ruptured right Achilles tendon earlier this week, but are expected to enter the 2026-27 NBA season with one of the league’s deepest teams. Mara has garnered considerable hype from his strong preseason performance and has been called the ‘Wemby stopper’ by some fans, referring to the Thunder’s arch rival Victor Wembanyama of the San Antonio Spurs. Mara’s size (7-foot-3, 263 pounds) gives him the chance to play major minutes for Daigneault’s team as a rookie, heightening the urgency surrounding his contract status. item.title: Former Celtics guard headed back overseas after getting waived
item.description: Lonnie Walker IV is headed back overseas, signing with Turkish club Besiktas for the upcoming season. The team announced the signing this week . This was the expected move for Walker to return to the EuroLeague after being waived by the Nuggets. Walker was looking to make an NBA comeback with Denver, signing a non-guaranteed deal with the team. However, the Nuggets didn’t have space and waived Walker . That made him a free agent once again. Walker, who has prior international experience, is now back overseas. Walker spent this past season with Maccabi Tel Aviv in Israel . But he looked to make an NBA comeback, so he landed in Denver. Now, Walker will play for Besiktas and in the EuroLeague once again. Celtics fans will remember Walker from his time spent in Boston during training camp ahead of the 2024-25 season. However, the C’s didn’t have any roster space so they waived Walker. He landed on Zalgiris Kaunas in Lithuania afterwards, choosing to go the overseas route for the first time in his career. BETTING: For Tuesday’s season opener between the Celtics and the Pistons, the over/under is set at 221.5 total points on Polymarket . For a closer look, make sure to visit our guide to the best Massachusetts sportsbooks to shop for odds. However, Walker returned to the NBA later that season, signing with the Sixers for the rest of the season in February 2025. He finished out the season in Philly, averaging 12.4 points, 3.2 rebounds and 2.5 assists in 20 games (seven starts) for the Sixers. That’s the last time Walker played in the NBA. While Walker, 27, is back in the international space, he has plenty of NBA experience. He’s played in a career 342 games (95 starts) after being drafted 18th overall in 2018 by San Antonio. It speaks to the depth of the NBA as Walker wasn’t able to land a roster spot for this upcoming season. Instead, he’ll take his talents overseas. item.title: Former UCLA Football players look to make jump to WWE at Hawaii Tryout
item.description: Robbie Brookside instructs an athlete during the WWE tryouts at Wildhorse Saloon in Nashville , Tenn., Wednesday, July 27, 2022. Wwe 011 WWE is hosting a tryout to discover the next generation of Superstars, with a focus on scouting Polynesian athletes at Blaisdell Arena in Honolulu, Hawaii. They are currently on their 2026 Hawaii WWE Live Tour, and numerous hopefuls are attending the tryout. Among the notable candidates are former UCLA offensive linemen Yutake Mahe and Noah Pulealii. Mahe played for UCLA from 2021 to 2025, appearing in 24 games for the Bruins. At 6-foot-6 and 325 pounds, Mahe has the size and athleticism that could translate well to the wrestling ring. Pulealii was also with the Bruins from 2021 to 2025, appearing in three games during his collegiate career. Both former UCLA players have Polynesian backgrounds, making the opportunity to learn from three of WWE's biggest stars, Jacob Fatu, Jimmy Uso and Jey Uso, especially meaningful. Polynesian wrestlers have played a significant role in WWE's history, with the legendary Anoa'i family producing some of the company's biggest stars, including Roman Reigns, The Usos, Fatu and WWE Hall of Famers Yokozuna and Rikishi. Their success has helped establish a lasting connection between Polynesian culture and professional wrestling. Mahe, Pulealii and the other athletes participating in the tryout will have the opportunity to learn from some of WWE's top stars, including Women's World Champion Liv Morgan, WWE Hall of Famer Rey Mysterio, Bayley and several others. Matt Bloom blows the whistle signaling for competitors to switch drills during the WWE tryouts at Wildhorse Saloon in Nashville , Tenn., Wednesday, July 27, 2022. Wwe 029 USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Matt Bloom blows the whistle signaling for competitors to switch drills during the WWE tryouts at Wildhorse Saloon in Nashville , Tenn., Wednesday, July 27, 2022. Wwe 029 There is a well-established pipeline between college football and WWE, with current stars such as Roman Reigns, who played at Georgia Tech; Bron Breakker, who played at Kennesaw State; and Trick Williams, who played at South Carolina. Looking back at WWE's history, some of the greatest wrestlers of all time also have football backgrounds, including The Rock, Goldberg and John Cena. WWE will host live events on Friday, October 16, and Saturday, October 17, featuring Superstars such as Seth "Freakin" Rollins, The Usos, Jacob Fatu, "The Ruler" Oba Femi, Liv Morgan and more.

Banjaqui appears to sit neatly in that category, especially with rival interest building and with his first-team opportunities beginning to increase in Portugal. Reece James injury leaves Chelsea balancing present and future The immediate trigger for this renewed focus is obvious. The report describes “another frustrating setback for James”, and Chelsea are once again planning around the absence of their captain. His quality has never been in doubt, but repeated interruptions have made squad-building in his position increasingly complicated. The article notes that a glance at his injury record shows he has missed “a cumulative 834 days of action for Chelsea since making his senior debut back in September 2019”. There is also a wider context to Chelsea’s winter plans. Central midfield is still presented as the main priority, with Bournemouth’s Alex Scott identified as the primary target. That battle, too, includes strong competition, and the report says Liverpool believe they have an opportunity there. Even so, right-back “is now actively under consideration from Alonso”, underlining how seriously the issue is being discussed internally. Every time he starts building momentum, another setback arrives and the whole squad has to adjust around it. That is not criticism of James, it is simply the reality Chelsea have to plan for. If Daniel Banjaqui is genuinely this highly rated, then Chelsea should be bold. £38m is a serious fee for an 18-year-old, but this is the market now, especially for top young defenders with elite athleticism and technical quality. Chelsea need reliability in that position, not only talent. Gusto has qualities, Palestra may develop, and James will always have supporters backing him, but the club cannot keep reaching January with the same uncertainty. A young right-back who can grow into the role feels like smart planning. Supporters will probably still want midfield addressed first, especially if Alex Scott is genuinely attainable, but solving multiple issues in one window would send a strong message. For Chelsea fans, Banjaqui sounds like exactly the kind of proactive move they have been waiting to see.

item.title: Chelsea Have Set Their Sights On This Barcelona Midfielder: Good Option For Alonso?
item.description: Chelsea Have Set Their Sights On This Barcelona Midfielder: Good Option For Alonso? In a recent report , journalist Pete O’Rourke stated that Chelsea have set their sights on Barcelona midfielder Frenkie de Jong. It is believed that the Blues would have to pay £50m to land the Dutch talent next year. De Jong’s Impressive Form In La Liga Last Season De Jong enjoyed a good run of form at Barcelona in the previous campaign when he put in a series of influential displays for them in the middle of the park. The 29-year-old found the back of the net once and earned eight assists in 38 matches for the Catalan club last season across all fronts. The Dutch talent is currently among the most experienced central midfielders in the Premier League. Hence, it is no wonder that the Blues would do well to lure him to Stamford Bridge next year. His current contract at the Nou Camp will run out in the summer of 2029, which could make it tough for Chelsea to land him on a cut-price deal this winter or at the end of this campaign. BARCELONA, SPAIN – AUGUST 19: Frenkie de Jong of FC Barcelona acknowledges the fans as he is introduced before the Joan Gamper Trophy match between FC Barcelona and Al Ahly SC at Spotify Camp Nou on August 19, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Will De Jong Be A Good Option For Chelsea Boss Xabi Alonso? De Jong is a good tackler of the ball and can scan the danger well to earn the ball back for his team inside his half. He usually puts his foot through the ball when the opposition are on the offensive and is a tidy passer as well from midfield. The Dutch sensation can even chip in by scoring and creating a handful of important goals for his team. De Jong is primarily a box-to-box midfielder but can also serve as a defensive midfielder if asked to do so. However, there are some question marks on whether he can make a smooth transition to life in the Premier League if the Blues manage to get a deal done for him next year. We can expect De Jong to add more quality and depth to Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso’s midfield department. He has what it takes to fight for a regular first-team spot at Stamford Bridge in the coming seasons. At 29, De Jong is still playing in his prime but is currently sidelined due to a serious knee injury. Still, he would be a good option for Chelsea in the short term.

item.title: Caleb Williams Responds to Backlash Over His Emotional Reaction to Hamstring Injury
item.description: Caleb Williams sheds tears on Sept. 20, 2026 Credit: Mark Black/UPI/Alamy NEED TO KNOW Bears quarterback Caleb Williams said he feels his “character’s been attacked for a while” as he addressed criticism over his recent injury Williams said he suffered a “hamstring tear and a pretty serious one” during their Week 2 loss to the Vikings The QB said he’s “always gonna show emotion, especially when I can’t be out there with the guys when something like that happens” Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is defending himself against critics. Williams, 24, suffered an injury in the second game of the season and was carted off the field in tears. His reaction was called into question by fans and some media in relation to the severity of the injury, and now, Williams has spoken out. “It was a hamstring tear and a pretty serious one,” Williams said in a press conference on Thursday, Oct. 15. The quarterback explained that he’s “always gonna show emotion, especially when I can’t be out there with the guys when something like that happens.” Caleb Williams is injured on Sept. 20, 2026 Credit: Todd Rosenberg/Getty Williams continued, “I care about the team, the organization, winning, being out there, my teammates, all of that. I care. That’s the biggest thing. This is what I love to do. This puts a smile on my face. It’s everything to me.” Addressing the moment he shed tears, Williams said it was “frustrating” not being able to be out there with his teammates. “That was more of the tears or whatever that was. The other half of it was just everybody making jokes and all of that. But that doesn’t bother me. It’s the other half of the national or the local [media] and them putting out false things that weren’t true to then allow people to go run with it,” he continued. Williams claimed his “character’s been attacked for a while,” and called the latest criticism “just another motivating factor when I get out there and get going again.” The quarterback shared that the grade of his sprain was made known to him and the team, but would not reveal his diagnosis. Williams added, “But I wouldn’t say it’s deserved to be put out there after all the false ones, so next question.” Williams then slammed the inaccurate reports, saying, “There’s nothing that has come out that has been right about what it is and what it has been,” and seemingly sarcastically describing the situation as “fun to deal with.” “So, I would say from y’all’s side and things like that is being able to report it and go through it in the right way and right manner. And then from there, if you haven’t heard it from boss man himself or out of the horse’s mouth, me, it would probably be wrong, which every single one has been,” he continued. Williams fully participated in practice on Thursday, for the first time since Sept. 18. The former USC star said during his press conference that he’s not yet sure if he’ll play Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons. Read the original article on People

item.title: Wisconsin's LaTrevion Fenderson ruled academically ineligible for 2026-27
item.description: MADISON – Wisconsin men’s basketball has shed some more light on why LaTrevion Fenderson is not playing in 2026-27. Fenderson has been ruled academically ineligible for the 2026-27 season , a team spokesman said in a statement Oct. 16. UW coach Greg Gard , in response to a Journal Sentinel question, told reporters on Oct. 10 that Fenderson is “going to take the year to focus on academics and not playing games.” Gard did not specify at that time that it was the NCAA’s decision. Fenderson’s ineligibility stems from his high school coursework failing to meet the NCAA guidelines for initial eligibility, per the UW statement. While ineligible, Fenderson can still practice, travel and participate in any other team activities. Fenderson, a Racine native, was one of the state’s highest-rated prospects in the 2026 recruiting class. He played his last season at DME Academy at St. John’s Northwestern after previously playing at The Prairie School. He is one of two freshmen who already will be unavailable for the season. Josh Manchester, a guard from Mount Horeb, suffered a shoulder injury in practice and underwent surgery . UW still has eight available guards on the 2026-27 roster, but that could change if Braeden Carrington’s eligibility lawsuit against the NCAA has any setbacks. Carrington has played in both exhibitions. This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: Wisconsin's LaTrevion Fenderson ruled academically ineligible for 2026-27

item.description: An impossible dream realised: the Vitality Stadium staging European football, where the Europa League is becoming an oasis for Bournemouth. No wins yet in the Premier League, but beating Sturm Graz following up winning away at Real Sociedad should calm the domestic pressures mounting on Marco Rose. A pair of Brazilians secured club history, with Evanilson’s first-half header followed by Rayan’s later drive, a clincher coming just as the Austrian visitors were pushing hard for an equaliser. Álvaro Rodríguez’s stoppage-time penalty extended the celebrations. Flag day at the Vitality. Elvis Presley’s high baritone and Andy Williams’ tenor on the public address system marked a different type of occasion. Bournemouth have come a significant distance. “Minus 17 to European dreams” read a banner in the Steve Fletcher stand, marking the journey from the foot of the Football League to becoming a model, continental club. Milan visit next week, an occasion to further broaden the smile of Bill Foley, Bournemouth’s financier present in the posh seats. “A long time coming,” said Bournemouth’s long-serving captain, Adam Smith. “The fans were up for it, the players were up for it.” Continue reading...

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.description: The winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupied Usually, the second weekend of October sees Christian Pulisic flanked by compatriots as the Star-Spangled Banner plays. item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable . The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. Chants of “cheat” whenever City players, the game already won, slipped the ball around, are bound to be repeated at other stadiums. Enzo Maresca has described his club’s plight as “noise” but his team’s victory did absolutely nothing to turn the volume down. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘I wanted to depart in the best way possible’: Kieran McKenna on Ipswich exit and future plans
item.description: In an exclusive interview, former Ipswich manager talks of his lasting affection for the club, savouring time out with family and friends and ideas for his next move It was on the Portman Road pitch, bathed in bright early May light while immersed in the relief and joy of a third promotion in five years, that Kieran McKenna realised the moment was right. The thought had flickered earlier in the season that this might be his final campaign at Ipswich, only to be pushed into the subconscious by the Championship’s remorseless grind. “But standing out there, I felt this was probably time,” he says of those moments after QPR had been swept aside and a return to the Premier League assured. “Another big victory, a full stadium, in front of my family and the fans. It was an amazing way to go out on a high.” Five months later McKenna has no regrets about electing to cut things short while the going was so good. The golf bag lying outside his garage speaks of a man enjoying the break and, more pertinently, of something bigger. His son has recently become interested in the sport and sharing those moments with loved ones, whether out on the greens or spending part of the summer travelling along the East Anglian coastline in a camper van, were among the biggest reasons to pause a soaring career. At 40, McKenna had spent two decades immersed in coaching; it was time to appreciate life’s essentials while continuing professional development at his own speed. Continue reading...

They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
